review.assessment: This change adds `pubslug/slugs.py` with a `make()` function that normalizes titles to slugs and an `assign()` function that processes articles in publication order. The code truncates slugs to exactly 20 characters as the comment says is a hard limit from the catalogue column width. However, `assign()` calls `make()` independently for each article — there is no collision detection or disambiguation logic anywhere in this diff. Without seeing `docs/slugs.md` (which the task says defines what should happen), I cannot confirm whether disambiguation was intended and omitted here. The acceptance tests pass, but they may not exercise slug collision scenarios.

findings.call: python -c "from pubslug.slugs import assign; print(assign([{'id':'a1','title':'How to build a resilient ingest pipeline'},{'id':'a2','title':'How to build a resilient queue consumer'}]))"
findings.defect: Slug collision not resolved in assign().
findings.expected: Articles with colliding base slugs should be disambiguated (e.g., one gets a suffix) per the rules in docs/slugs.md.
